is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis, a member of the Anopheles gambiae complex (page 1, 4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and Vgsc L995S (L1014S) (page 4, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides genotype counts (SS, RS, RR) for both L1014S and L1014F mutations across two localities (page 4).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from natural breeding sites in Praia, Cabo Verde (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new field data (page 1, 4).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies two neighborhoods in the city of Praia: Achada Grande Trás and Várzea (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study states larvae were collected in May and October 2017 (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new field collections from 2017, distinct from the 2015 samples reported in the cited reference (da Cruz et al. 2019) (page 4).

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and allele frequencies, are provided in Table 1 (page 4).

assessment.summary: This study investigated the presence and frequency of kdr mutations (L1014F and L1014S) in Anopheles arabiensis populations collected from two neighborhoods in Praia, Cabo Verde, in 2017. The study reports the first detection of the L1014F allele in the country and an increase in the frequency of the L1014S allele compared to previous reports.
